title: [urlSync] create widget

comments.body: API updated @vvo
Great, do we also do the `useHash` parameter in 0.0.1? There will be implementation that will only want to use the hash `#` and not the query string one (example: magento)
that will have to be done I guess :)
So maybe in 1.0.0 :-)

Could be cool to have a function that is able to generate an url from a "state".

Ex for magento: for now I need to do something like :

```
'#q=&page=0&refinements=%5B%7B%22categories%22%3A%5B%22'.$path.'%22%5D%7D%5D&numerics_refinements=%7B%7D&index_name=%22'.$indexName.'%22';
```

Could be cool to say something like:

``` php
generateUrl({
 'refinements':<?php echo json_encode(['categories' => $path]); ?>,
 'index_name': '<?php echo $indexName; ?>'
}
```

Also could be cool to have only what is needed in the hash/url.

For example if there is no refinements the hash would be :

```
#q=query
```

And going on page 2 would be:

```
#q=query&p=2
```

I too would like to have this kind of feature @maxiloc. We discussed it in the helper and also with @bobylito but I can't remember why we decided not to do it.

What is your use case, where will you use it?
I don't see why we wouldn't be able to do that. I think that it was related to the helper scope not the instantsearch.js scope...

I have a few remarks on this one.

> The url sync needs to override the defaults parameter set by any other components. So it should always come last in the initialisation.

Do you suggest we automatically push it last in the list, or that we educate users into adding the widget last in their code?

> The update should take place each time there is an update of the SearchParameters

I would have done it everytime we call `search` on the helper instead. This is a tiny difference but this makes more sense as the url should reflect the state of the current display of the page (which is not triggered until we `search()`)

Also, even if we use the default queryString, we should pack all our data in one variable, as to not collide with variables already defined in our customer implementation. 

I think the state->string and string->state logic should be in the helper, but the url synchronisation and load should be in the widget.

> I think the state->string and string->state logic should be in the helper, but the url synchronisation and load should be in the widget.

:+1:

> Do you suggest we automatically push it last in the list, or that we educate users into adding the widget last in their code?

Yes (I know it's kinda ugly :P)

> I think the state->string and string->state logic should be in the helper, but the url synchronisation and load should be in the widget.

I partially agree here. I think the helper should provide a way to get a meaningful subset of the state for serialization purpose, but not the serialization process itself. The serialization is part of the url mechanism as well. If we use other forms of storage, then the string wouldn't be meaningful but the sub object will always be.

state -> partial state + partial state -> state >> Helper
partial state -> string vice versa, >> Widget

> I partially agree here. I think the helper should provide a way to get a meaningful subset of the state for serialization purpose, but not the serialization process itself. The serialization is part of the url mechanism as well. If we use other forms of storage, then the string wouldn't be meaningful but the sub object will always be.

I would still add to the helper those two methods:
- setStateFromQueryString
- getStateAsQueryString

Mostly because this will allow us from the autocomplete.js project to generate urls that will be compatible with the urlsync widget of instantsearch.js (from an autocomplete suggestion, link to an instant search results, what we frequently do).

Otherwise we would have to tell the autocomplete.js to somehow use the instantsearch.js project (and make it a dependency or something) to generate urls.

There will also be a good usage from the server side to do server side rendering and burn instantsearch.js urls in the html.

All of this is also doable if the methods are somewhere in instantsearch.js but I would find it weird from a usage POV (maybe show how it would be used from the instantsearch.js @bobylito?).

I do not see why the state <-> querystring serialization mechanism should not be in the helper?

> state -> partial state + partial state -> state >> Helper
> partial state -> string vice versa, >> Widget

Did not get it.

> Yes (I know it's kinda ugly :P)

Yes to what? :)

As @vvo suggested, maybe a `urlSync: true` could be a better API for the widget that does not do any DOM manipulation or rendering

Just tested it, it looks great. I have 1 question and 1 issue.
Question: is that expected that even with a threshold of 5 seconds the url update instantly ?
Issue: When you type fast on the search input with url sync enable, sometimes you loose focus.
We'll also need to avoid adding query parameters if they have no values (like `refinements=[]` or `numericRefinements={}`, `page=0`)
@redox Maybe we can open another issue here?

By default when loading I have this: `http://localhost:8080/#q=&idx=instant_search&p=0`

What would you want to remove? q and p ?

> By default when loading I have this: http://localhost:8080/#q=&idx=instant_search&p=0

Just tested it on the Magento integration, and we had also all the `refinements`. I'm OK keeping `p` and `q`.

> Just tested it on the Magento integration, and we had also all the refinements. I'm OK keeping p and q.

Wait, it seems to be caused by our PHP code actually :)
